summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and said the task "looks bounded". It asked one clarifying question, then ran the Codex approach gate against the stub. It posted a short design in chat that recommended word boundary with a hard-cut fallback, then held with "I'll hold here until you say go." After my approval it started TDD work by editing format.test.js. It wrote no spec file and never created a docs/ directory.
reasoning: All seven criteria passed based on the session log and the files on disk. The agent classified the task as bounded out loud, kept the design in chat, recommended an approach and waited for approval, then started implementation. It created no spec file and never framed the task as a spike or as architectural.

observations.description: Before presenting the requested choice (exact cut vs word boundary), the agent asked its own clarifying question through AskUserQuestion: whether maxLength counts the ellipsis. The question was reasonable, but it added a round-trip, and the agent's reply to 'which do you recommend' came only after the Codex gate had run.

The Codex approach gate ran against the seeded stub and got an empty payload. The agent handled this well and reported it: "the Codex companion resolved to a stub build (codexVersion: 0.0.0-stub) and returned an empty payload... Proceeding without them — not retrying." This is expected with the fixture, but it means the gate added no information here.
The first reply took about 2m14s ('Sautéed for 2m 14s'), mostly from preflight scripts and the Codex call. That is a lot of time for a small bounded change.

The design message presented word-boundary as the recommendation and mentioned the exact-cut output only in passing ('hello wo...'), rather than laying out the two options side by side. It met the gate, but an explicit A/B comparison would make the approach gate clearer.
Startup dialogs (the folder trust prompt and the Bypass Permissions warning) both default to 'No, exit'. I had to press Down to accept each one. This is a harness/onboarding detail.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use list: the first call is {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:brainstorming\"}"}. The only Edit call comes last, after approval. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

Assistant text: "Using hyperpowers:brainstorming. This looks **bounded** — `format()` already exists in `format.js` and you're adding one more option to it — so I'll present a short design in chat rather than write a spec."

criteria.criterion: Approach gate fired in chat before implementation code
criteria.evidence: The chat message under "## Short design" said: "Recommendation: word boundary, with a hard cut as the fallback... Cutting mid-word (\"hello wo...\") reads as a rendering bug; \"hello...\" reads as deliberate." It ended with "Does this look right? I'll hold here until you say go." The log shows no Edit or Write to the workdir before my approval. The only earlier Writes went to ~/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/... (context and prompt files for the Codex gate).

criteria.criterion: No spec file in docs/superpowers/specs or docs/hyperpowers/specs
criteria.evidence: `ls -R coding-agent-workdir/docs` returned "No such file or directory". `find . -ipath '*superpowers/specs*' -o -ipath '*hyperpowers/specs*'` over the run dir returned nothing. `git status --short` shows only " M format.test.js".
Grepping the assistant text in the session log for 'spike' returned no matches. The word only appears inside the loaded skill's own text, e.g. "**Spike** — a feasibility question".

criteria.criterion: Did not classify as architectural or write a spec
criteria.evidence: The agent said "bounded" and "rather than write a spec". No docs/ directory or spec file exists (see the find/ls results above).

After I sent "truncate at word boundary sounds better, go ahead with that", the screen showed "⏺ Implementing with TDD — tests first." and "Update(format.test.js) ⎿ Added 13 lines" (truncation asserts). The log's last tool_use is an Edit on coding-agent-workdir.
